thread:
Maya R.: Hey team — customer (acct: acme-corp) hitting 400s from /v1/rerank. They say it started after a client-side change. Full error: '400 Bad Request - malformed rerank request'. They attached the request body.

Devon L.: Can you paste the exact request body they sent?

Maya R.: Pasted from their logs: ```
POST /v1/rerank 
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "query": "Which option is best?",
  "candidates": ["opt1", "opt2"],
  "top_k": null,
  "ids": "1234",
  "metadata": {}
}
```

Maya R.: Response body: ```
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Invalid request body: top_k must be an integer > 0",
    "code": 400
  }
}
```

Priya K.: Two obvious issues: top_k null and ids is a string instead of array. Our validator should catch both and return clearer messages about types. Does customer expect top_k optional?

Maya R.: Customer claims previous client versions omitted top_k fine (defaults to 5). They say their SDK changed shape to send null for unset fields.

Devon L.: That explains it. We currently validate presence of top_k and enforce integer >0. Older behavior tolerated missing field by using default. We changed strictness in last validation PR (safety hardening). Need to confirm behavior expected for missing vs null.

oncall-bot: Deployment note: validation middleware v2.3.1 rolled to prod 2026-02-28 03:12 UTC (canary -> 100%).

Priya K.: Proposed mitigation: accept null as absent (treat as default) and add explicit type error for ids to indicate expected array. Also add a migration note in SDK docs about null vs omitted fields.

Devon L.: Quick patch idea: in request normalization layer: if top_k is null -> delete field (let default apply). For ids, if typeof ids === 'string' -> try to parse comma-separated? I'd rather return a helpful 400 telling them to send ["1234"]; auto-coercion is risky.

Maya R.: Customer wants a workaround now. They can strip nulls from payload or pin SDK to previous release. Which is fastest?

Devon L.: Fastest is server-side tweak for top_k null -> accept. Add a clearer error message for bad ids. I'll assemble a small patch and a rolling deploy.

Devon L.: Patch diff (sketch): ```js
// normalize request
if (req.body.top_k === null) delete req.body.top_k; // fallback to default
if (req.body.ids && typeof req.body.ids === 'string') {
  throw new BadRequest('ids must be an array of strings, e.g. ["id1", "id2"]');
}
```

Priya K.: Add unit test for both cases and update API docs to say: top_k optional, null treated as omitted.

Devon L.: Rolling canary now. Will monitor errors.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for service=rerank-validator image=rerank-validator:fix-null-topk-20260310, canary=10%

Maya R.: I'll tell the customer to either remove top_k or wait a few minutes while you canary. Also give them the explicit ids error text so they can check their client.

Devon L.: Canary looks clean at 10%. No new 400 spikes. Promoting to 50%...

Devon L.: Promoted to 100%. Patch live.

Maya R.: Customer confirmed after removing nulls they no longer see 400s. They will patch their SDK too.

Priya K.: Follow-ups: 1) Update SDK docs and changelog. 2) Add a small telemetry counter for 'bad_ids_type' to proactively alert. 3) Add a note in changelog about stricter validation in v2.3.x so teams know why nulls break things.

Maya R.: Marking support ticket resolved for now. Will keep the thread open for the docs PR. :thumbsup:
